headline: Florida Sues OpenAI and Sam Altman Over Alleged ChatGPT Safety Failures
raw_snippet: Florida filed a landmark 83-page civil complaint on June 1 accusing OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman of deceptive trade practices, negligence, product liability violations, and public nuisance. The lawsuit alleges ChatGPT aided mass shooters (including the FSU shooting), encouraged suicide in vulnerable users, and addicted children. Florida is the first U.S. state to sue OpenAI and the first to seek to hold an AI CEO personally liable for user harm.

headline: Florida AG Launches Parallel Criminal Investigation Into OpenAI Over FSU Shooting
raw_snippet: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier is conducting a separate criminal investigation into OpenAI over the FSU shooter's alleged consultation of ChatGPT before the April 2025 attack. The AG stated that 'if it was a person on the other end of that screen, we would be charging them with murder.' The state says OpenAI could face potentially billions of dollars in damages across civil and criminal proceedings.

headline: OpenAI Frontier Models and Codex Now Generally Available on AWS via Amazon Bedrock
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced that GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, and Codex are now generally available on Amazon Bedrock, opening a new path for millions of AWS customers to build with OpenAI through existing security, compliance, procurement, billing, and governance workflows. GPT-5.5 is available in US East (Ohio) and GPT-5.4 in US East (Ohio) and US West (Oregon). OpenAI plans future availability for Daybreak on AWS.

headline: OpenAI Launches Rosalind Biodefense Program for Pandemic Preparedness
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched Rosalind Biodefense, a program that sponsors access to GPT-Rosalind for vetted developers building frontier biosecurity applications and extends access to select U.S. government and allied public-health partners. Partners include Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (protein engineering) and CEPI (vaccine design for the '100 Days Mission'). The program has a developer track and a government track for outbreak-response planning, diagnostics, and medical countermeasure development.

headline: Advanced Account Security Required for Cyber Model Access Starting June 1
raw_snippet: Beginning June 1, 2026, individual members of Trusted Access for Cyber accessing OpenAI's most cyber-capable and permissive models are required to enable Advanced Account Security with phishing-resistant protections. Organizations with trusted access can attest to phishing-resistant authentication as part of their single sign-on workflow. This security deadline affects GPT-5.5-Cyber and other permissive cybersecurity models.

headline: Codex Expands Beyond Developers with Role-Specific Plugins, Sites, and Annotations
raw_snippet: OpenAI shipped a major Codex expansion with six role-specific plugins (sales, data analytics, creative production, product design, public equity investing, and investment banking), Codex Sites for creating interactive hosted apps and dashboards, and expanded Annotations for documents, spreadsheets, and slides. More than 5 million people now use Codex weekly, with non-developers growing 3x faster than developers. Codex integration into ChatGPT app announced for coming weeks.

headline: OpenAI Calls for Global Youth AI Safety Institute Ahead of G7 Summit
raw_snippet: OpenAI proposed an international youth safety institute to coordinate governments, researchers, civil society, and industry on raising youth AI safety standards. Published ahead of the G7 Leaders' Summit, the post outlines principles including privacy-preserving age estimation, default safeguards when age is uncertain, annual youth safety risk assessments, accessible parental controls, and stronger protocols for high-risk interactions like self-harm and exploitation.

headline: OpenAI Deprecates GPT Image Models (gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-image-1.5, chatgpt-image-latest)
raw_snippet: OpenAI notified developers that three older GPT Image models — gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-image-1.5, and chatgpt-image-latest — are deprecated and will be removed from the API on December 1, 2026. All three migrate to gpt-image-2. This comes after DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 retired on May 12, forcing developers who had migrated to gpt-image-1-mini to plan a second forced migration.

headline: Sam Altman Admits Anthropic Has Overtaken OpenAI in Enterprise AI Spending
raw_snippet: At OpenAI's 'Intelligence at Work' enterprise event on June 2, CEO Sam Altman disclosed that Anthropic has overtaken OpenAI in corporate AI spending among enterprise customers — the first time a rival has led OpenAI on that metric. Altman also revealed cost concerns are now the second most common complaint from enterprise customers, referencing a meme: 'The company spent its entire 2026 budget in Q1.' Anthropic's business adoption rose to 34.4% in April vs OpenAI's 32.3%.

headline: OpenAI's Top Token User Now Consuming 100 Billion Tokens per Month
raw_snippet: At the Intelligence at Work enterprise event, Sam Altman revealed OpenAI's top token user consumes approximately 100 billion tokens per month — a 1 million-fold increase from six years ago when the top user consumed about 100,000 tokens per month. Altman also noted this was not even the global token leader, saying someone else used even more.

headline: OpenAI Plans AI Tools for Finance and Legal Markets, Racing Anthropic
raw_snippet: Bloomberg reported that OpenAI is planning specialized AI tools for finance and legal markets as it races with Anthropic for enterprise dominance. The move accompanies the launch of Codex plugins for investment banking and public equity investing, with more role-specific plugins coming for corporate finance, private equity, marketing strategy, strategy consulting, and legal.

headline: GPT-5.5 Instant Gets Readability Upgrade — Shorter, Less Bullet-Heavy Responses
raw_snippet: OpenAI updated GPT-5.5 Instant in ChatGPT and the API to produce shorter, more natural responses with fewer bullet points. The update did not require an API version bump. Additionally, Canvas is being removed from GPT-5.5 Instant and GPT-5.5 Thinking — writing and coding tasks will now happen inside the main chat interface through 'special blocks' instead of a separate panel.

headline: OpenAI Confirms GPT-4.5 Retirement on June 27 and o3 Retirement on August 26
raw_snippet: OpenAI confirmed retirement dates for two older models in ChatGPT: GPT-4.5 will exit on June 27 after a 30-day sunset period, and o3 will exit on August 26 after a 90-day sunset period. Both retirements apply to ChatGPT only — there are no changes to API access. GPT-5 and GPT-5.3-Codex have fully superseded GPT-4.5 on every benchmark. The recommended reasoning replacement for o3 is o4.

headline: OpenAI Deprecates Evals Platform, Agent Builder, and Reusable Prompts
raw_snippet: OpenAI deprecated three developer products on June 3: (1) Evals platform — becomes read-only October 31, shuts down November 30, with migration to Promptfoo; (2) Agent Builder — shuts down November 30, migrate to Agents SDK or ChatGPT Workspace Agents; (3) Reusable Prompts (v1/prompts) — de-emphasized immediately, shuts down November 30. ChatKit remains available. Developers advised to move prompt content into application code.

headline: Sam Altman Meets with Lawmakers in DC, Presents AI Oversight Blueprint
raw_snippet: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman met with House Speaker Mike Johnson, Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, and Trump administration officials involved with the executive order on AI. Altman pushed for public-private AI collaboration and a greater role for OpenAI in NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation. House Speaker Johnson described the meeting as 'very good, productive' and discussed 'light touch' regulation.

headline: OpenAI Publishes Federal AI Governance Blueprint and Public Policy Agenda
raw_snippet: OpenAI released a blueprint titled 'Democratic Governance of Frontier AI' proposing a three-part federal framework: (1) building on emerging state frontier safety laws like California's SB 53; (2) strengthening CAISI as the primary federal AI safety institution; (3) mobilizing a broader government resilience plan for national security and public safety challenges. OpenAI stated 'democratic governments — not private companies acting alone — must ultimately determine the rules.' The paper diverged from the White House on some AI safety positions.

headline: OpenAI Introduces New GPT-Rosalind Capabilities for Life Sciences Research
raw_snippet: OpenAI updated the GPT-Rosalind series with a model combining GPT-5.5's agentic coding and tool-use capabilities with stronger intelligence in drug-discovery domains such as medicinal chemistry and genomics. The updated model uses 31% fewer tokens than GPT-5.5 for genomics analyses. OpenAI also launched Life Sciences Research and Life Sciences NGS Analysis plugins, bringing sourced evidence retrieval, biological interpretation, and bioinformatics execution into the same workspace.

headline: ChatGPT Dreaming V3: Major Memory Architecture Upgrade Rolls Out to Plus and Pro Users
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched Dreaming V3, its most significant ChatGPT memory upgrade since the original 2024 rollout. An asynchronous background process now synthesizes memory from many conversations simultaneously, automatically capturing context and updating memories as circumstances change (e.g., 'going to Singapore in July' rewrites to 'went to Singapore in July 2026'). 5x compute efficiency, 82.8% factual recall, 75.1% time-sensitive accuracy. Rolling out to Plus and Pro users in the US, with Free tier access planned.

headline: ChatGPT Conversion-Optimized Ads Begin Rolling Out to Advertisers
raw_snippet: OpenAI rolled out conversion-optimized campaigns in ChatGPT Ads Manager on June 5, transforming its advertising platform from a reach/traffic channel into a performance-based ecosystem. Advertisers can now optimize ad delivery toward users likely to complete actions like purchases or signups, using JavaScript Pixel and Conversions API measurement tools. The ChatGPT ad pilot crossed $100M in annualized revenue within six weeks of launching, with international expansion to Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

headline: OpenAI Targets September IPO at Up to $850 Billion Valuation
raw_snippet: Reports confirmed OpenAI is working with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley on a confidential IPO filing targeting a public debut as early as September 2026 at $730B-$850B valuation. OpenAI's annualized revenue has passed $20B (up from $6B in 2024) but internal projections suggest $14B in losses for 2026 alone, with profitability not expected until ~2030. This comes days after rival Anthropic confidentially filed its own draft S-1 on June 1 at a $965B valuation — for the first time surpassing OpenAI.

headline: OpenAI Expands GPT-5.5-Cyber Access to the European Union
raw_snippet: OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber reached EU cybersecurity teams, businesses, governments, and institutions including the EU AI Office under the EU Cyber Action Plan (announced May 11). The model is tuned for authorized security work including vulnerability identification, malware analysis, reverse engineering, and patch validation. Rival Anthropic opened its competing Mythos model to ENISA days later, intensifying the transatlantic AI cybersecurity competition.

headline: Codex Sites Launches in Preview for Business and Enterprise Customers
raw_snippet: Codex Sites entered preview, allowing business and enterprise customers to create and share interactive hosted websites and apps from prompts. Sites turn analysis into dashboards, planners, and lightweight tools shareable via URL within a workspace. Enterprise admins can enable Sites through admin settings, and ChatGPT Business workspaces include Sites by default. ChatGPT Enterprise admins can enable Sites through role-based access control (RBAC).

headline: Codex Investment Banking Plugin Launches with Institutional Data Integrations
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched an investment banking Codex plugin that syncs institutional market feeds including Moody's, Daloopa, Datasite, FactSet, LSEG, S&P, PitchBook, and Hebbia to streamline financial modeling, competitive landscaping, and pitch book preparation. Bankers can turn research and diligence into client-ready materials. More plugins are planned for corporate finance, private equity, marketing strategy, strategy consulting, and legal.

headline: Canadian Privacy Regulators Find OpenAI Violated PIPEDA with ChatGPT Training Data
source_name: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
raw_snippet: Canadian federal and provincial privacy commissioners released findings (May 6, continued coverage into June) from their joint investigation of OpenAI, concluding that ChatGPT's initial training did not comply with Canadian privacy laws. Deficiencies found in consent, transparency, accuracy, retention, access rights, and accountability. OpenAI scraped publicly accessible personal information and used user interactions for fine-tuning without valid consent. Alberta and BC regulators found some issues unresolved.

headline: OpenAI Canvas Removed from GPT-5.5 Instant and Thinking Models
raw_snippet: OpenAI removed Canvas from GPT-5.5 Instant and GPT-5.5 Thinking in ChatGPT. Writing and coding tasks now happen inside the main chat interface through inline 'writing blocks' and 'code blocks' rather than a separate panel. Paid users can continue using Canvas temporarily through legacy models until those models are sunset. This consolidation moves all structured content creation directly into the chat interface.
